statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-33846 (GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-1): GnuTLS before 3.8.13 does not check that DTLS handshake fragments claim a consistent message_length, and a missing array size check lets a remote peer overwrite heap memory. GnuTLS fixes it in 3.8.13 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html), and Alpine lists it as fixed in gnutls 3.8.13-r0 for 3.23 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-33846). This owner is built from Alpine's gnutls package source for 3.23. Its published gnutls packages for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, x86_64 and aarch64, are 3.8.11-r0 and 3.8.12-r0, whose libgnutls library reports GnuTLS 3.8.11 and 3.8.12, and the current 3.8.13-r0, whose library reports GnuTLS 3.8.13. The range ends at 3.8.13-r0.

CVE-2026-33846: merge_handshake_packet() in the GnuTLS DTLS handshake reassembly merged fragments without checking that message_length stayed the same, so crafted fragments could write past the allocated heap buffer. Upstream advisory GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-1 (https://www.gnutls.org/security-new.html#GNUTLS-SA-2026-04-29-1, https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/issues/1816) was fixed in GnuTLS 3.8.13 by https://gitlab.com/gnutls/gnutls/-/commit/65ab33fa54e34fba69d793735b7df3d383d1ff78 ("buffers: add more checks to DTLS reassembly"). Debian fixed it for trixie in gnutls28 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 (DSA-6281-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-33846), which applies the GnuTLS 3.8.13 security patch set to 3.8.9 and carries that upstream commit. The only build of this owner currently published for Debian 13 is made from that Debian version, and the changelog shipped in its libgnutls30t64 package on amd64 and arm64 lists CVE-2026-33846 under 3.8.9-3+deb13u4. The range ends at that build, the lowest published version carrying the fix. Builds made from Debian's earlier 3.8.9-3+deb13u2 and 3.8.9-3+deb13u3 sources predate the fix and sort below it, so they are reported as affected.
